submitter: bugfix_277_required_fields_repair lane — rendered_html_transform repair route (owner ruling 2026-08-20), CQ-028
rationale: bugs_open/277 §5 established, with a rendered measurement against production's own engine, that 7 literal_markdown findings (all `code_span`, all source=rendered_html, all on the `ported-page` slot) are unreachable by EVERY repair route this estate has: the component's content_data is 215 bytes of provenance metadata, its template's only field is {{.body}}, so 473's rerender regenerates from nothing and section_edit+strip strips a map with no prose — both inapplicable BY CONSTRUCTION. Migration 499 already replaced the escalation's named target with the routing TEST ('read the finding's source, ask whether content_data can reproduce rendered_html'). The owner ruled the same day, in chat: these findings DO get a repair route, and building one means a transform that edits finished HTML directly. This change builds that route with maximal reuse: a named deterministic transform (`x` -> x) carried by apply_section_edit as a third edit_type (inheriting its lock gate, RFC_015 decision gate, per-slot floors, regulated-identity refusal, single persist switch, reassembly, git_commit and Cloudflare deploy), routed by the detector at filing time using 499's test as code. New authority (writing rendered_html not derived from content_data) ships per the 2026-08-02 §2 owner ruling: an opt-in config key whose unsafe default is OFF, enabled by migration 513 on section-editor's apply_edit step only. The transform inserts ONLY the two fixed strings and around bytes already served as text — the literal_markdown.go 'never markdown->HTML' rule guards values feeding INTO the unescaping render pipe, and this operates on the pipe's OUTPUT, downstream, with an interior character class that excludes <, > and backtick so the inserted pair cannot misnest. Conversion is strictly narrower than detection, so anything detection flags that the transform cannot safely reach fails verification into the attempt ladder and a human — the safe direction, stated in code. The whole-page verifier (VerifyLiteralMarkdownResolved) is untouched and survives the re-route by its own design.

plan.summary: The estate's first finished-HTML repair, in three reusable parts plus routing and enablement: (1) datahelpers.ConvertLiteralCodeSpansInHTML — tokenizer byte-splice sharing the detector's exact skip set (same package, same nonAssertionElements map), mutation-proven against a real production fixture that carries both the live finding and an adversarial in-script JS template literal; (2) apply_section_edit edit_type rendered_html_transform — opt-in (allow_rendered_html_transform, default OFF), floors and regulated-identity guard enforced on the outgoing html, HTML-only persist (content_data structurally untouchable: nil takes updatePageComponentAfterEdit's html-only branch); (3) datahelpers.ContentDataCanFillTemplate — migration 499's routing test as code, deliberately coarse toward 'can fill' (= keep today's route); (4) check_literal_markdown routes per page via transformRouteSlot — section-editor IFF every finding is rendered_html-source code_span on ONE once-occurring slot whose component cannot regenerate, else page-rerender unchanged; (5) migration 513 (+ROLLBACK, round-tripped to the byte against the live row) enables the key and whitelists the transform_name input on section-editor's apply_edit only. item_type, item_key, producer set and verifier all unchanged. The new pair literal_markdown->section-editor starts at zero lifetime completes, so the 444 promoter holds it until one deliberate canary completes — the bootstrap this lane has performed by hand before (commit 8d77196ad).

edits.rationale: The transform itself, placed in the same package as the single-sourced pattern set AND the detector's parser skip-set so repairer and detector structurally cannot drift. Tokenizer splice, not parse+re-serialise: html.Parse wraps fragments in <html><body> and normalises the whole document, on a component whose rendered_html is the ONLY copy of its content. converted==0 implies byte-identical output. TESTS (rendered_html_code_spans_test.go + testdata/ported_page_tool_cubic_bezier.html, same commit): Four contract legs: repair contract (post-transform, the detector's own scan — ExtractAssertionText + LiteralMarkdownPatterns — finds nothing) proven on REAL production bytes (tool-cubic-bezier's 8,743-byte rendered_html, which carries the live `ease-in-out` finding AND a `left 1s ${css}` template literal inside <script> that an unguarded regex would corrupt); conversion ⊆ detection property; splice fidelity (byte-identity when converted==0, single-substitution reconstruction when 1); skip-set parity with deliberately MIXED-CASE tags to catch the TagName buffer-mutation reorder. Both guards mutation-proven: reorder -> 'script mixed' case fails; skip disabled -> 3 tests fail including the fixture's script literal.
edits.sketch: z := html.NewTokenizer(...); for each token: StartTag/EndTag -> out.Write(z.Raw()) THEN TagName() (ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: TagName() lower-cases the tag bytes IN PLACE in the buffer Raw() aliases — found building this, mutation-proven, recorded in the file header and CQ-028); maintain skipDepth over nonAssertionElements; TextToken outside skips -> codeSpanConvertRe = `([A-Za-z0-9][^`<>\n]{0,80})` replaced with $1.

edits.rationale: Migration 499's routing test as code, so the detector can apply it at filing time. Deliberately coarse toward 'can fill' — a false 'can fill' costs a refused rerender and a human escalation (today's behaviour); a false 'cannot fill' would aim the HTML edit at a component whose content_data keeps the defect for its next regeneration to reprint. The regex misses function-arg and variable-bound fields BY DESIGN: missing a field shrinks the list, which can only push toward the safe verdict.
edits.sketch: templateTopLevelFieldRe = \{\{-?\s*(?:(?:range|with|if)\s+)?\.([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*) ; CanFill = no fields (static) OR any field present non-nil non-empty in content_data. Tests include the worked case: provenance-only map vs {{.body}} template -> false.

edits.symbol: ApplySectionEditInputSpec (+transform_name optional, +allow_rendered_html_transform config key), applyRenderedHTMLTransform, persist switch case
edits.rationale: Reuse over new machinery: this action already owns every control the route needs, and the owned-page guard's own prose names section-editor as how owned pages are legitimately edited. The gate is a CONFIG KEY, not an input, so a caller cannot grant itself the authority (2026-08-02 §2). Every refusal is an ERROR, not a skip — config-off, unknown transform, empty rendered_html, and converted==0 all route to the attempt ladder and a human; a skip would read as success to check_edit_skipped. converted==0 in particular refuses rather than deploying identical bytes and reporting an edit ('complete is not proof' made structural). The persist case wires enforceSingleSlotFloors + refuseRegulatedIdentityEdit exactly as content_edit does (the floors coverage test reads this file and passes on its merits), then updatePageComponentAfterEdit(pcID, html, nil) — the pre-existing html-only branch, so the transform is structurally unable to write content_data. Optional-key budget: apply_section_edit 6 -> 7 of N=10 (WFA-013 audit run; cron literal regenerated, parity test green). The design-principle header states the exception rather than implying it: this edits the render OUTPUT of components with no source of truth to edit, and nothing regenerates them — the same property that made them unrepairable is what makes the edit durable.
edits.sketch: case "rendered_html_transform": outcome, err = applyRenderedHTMLTransform(pcData, inputs, params.StepConfig.Config, logger) — gate check; switch transform_name { case "code_span_to_code_tag": out, n, err := datahelpers.ConvertLiteralCodeSpansInHTML(existingHTML); n==0 -> error }. Result map gains transform_name/transform_converted (durable record, the StrippedMarkdownFields precedent).

edits.symbol: transformRouteSlot, Run (query +LEFT JOIN content_components for html_template; per-page slot metadata; handler + spec extras)
edits.rationale: Routing decided by the detector at filing time — the one place that holds the findings, the content_data and (now) the template together. ALL conditions must hold to leave the default: every finding rendered_html-source AND code_span AND one named slot occurring exactly once AND ContentDataCanFillTemplate false. item_type/item_key/verifier untouched; the verifier's whole-page zero-findings remit is exactly what the transform must achieve to complete. Old-shape open items are unaffected (dedup holds them until terminal; the wont_fix loop then re-files at the new shape — self-healing, slower). Same commit: handler_coverage_test.go gains section-editor in knownHandlerAgents (verified live before the line: 83 lifetime completes) and check_literal_markdown.go in computedHandlerAgentSites, per that guard's own contract; and check_literal_markdown_routing_test.go holds the routing unit tests (fires on the worked case; 11 refusal directions each land on the default).
edits.sketch: handlerAgent := "page-rerender"; if slot, ok := transformRouteSlot(pf.Findings, slotsByPage[pf.PageID]); ok { handlerAgent = "section-editor"; spec[edit_type/transform_name/slot_name/fix] = ... }. Unit tests: fires on the worked case; 11 refusal directions each land on the default.

edits.symbol: allow_rendered_html_transform=true + input_fields += transform_name on section-editor.apply_edit (+ ROLLBACK file)
edits.rationale: The entire enablement surface, 474's idiom exactly (snapshot_agent, action-anchored jsonb_set, needle gates, DO/RAISE positive-presence verify — no negative-form comparison, so no NULL reads green). input_fields is ExtractActionInputs' Strategy-1 WHITELIST (action_inputs.go:831), so the transform_name entry is load-bearing plumbing, not decoration. Round-tripped against the live row: apply -> rollback -> md5 identical to the pre-image (fdb8cb4d... both sides); then applied for real. Ordering safe both sides of the roll, stated in the header: old binary reads neither key; a new-shape item in the config-gap window fails loudly into the attempt ladder and succeeds on retry.
edits.sketch: two anchored UPDATEs + DO block asserting flag true on exactly 1 live row and transform_name present exactly once (element count, not row count, so a double-append cannot read green).

grounded_in: [1] The population and its unreachability: bugs_open/277 §5.1-§5.3 — all 7 findings source=rendered_html, pattern=code_span, slot=ported-page; content_data is {schema,sha256,source,qa_tier,generator} (215 bytes); template's only field is {{.body}}; rendered with production's engine and Option(missingkey=zero): owned payload 4,665B out, 0 visible chars, err=<nil>; generic control 11,035B with 6,568B of prose. Fleet census: 115 instances, 100 missing body, split total across rebuild_policy.

[2] The owner rulings this implements: (a) 2026-08-20, chat, this session: 'Do those seven findings get a repair route? Building one means a transform that edits finished HTML directly - I think yes.' (b) 2026-08-02 §2 (CLAUDE.md): 'when a seam's widest branch is licensed by callers-must-all-be-X, make X a field with the unsafe default OFF' — implemented as the allow_rendered_html_transform config key. (c) Migration 499's live pre_query (md5 0d72b423..., len 13938): the routing test this automates.

[3] Why section-editor is the legitimate carrier for owned pages: owned_page_guard.go header — 'migration 164 says in terms that re-assembly of existing page_components is deliberately NOT gated — it is how owned pages deploy'; its review-item fix prose names 'edit via apply_section_edit/section-editor'. Measured: section_edit -> section-editor is 36 complete / 1 failed on rebuild_policy='owned' (live + archive, 2026-08-20). LANDMINES 'guard cover follows output_field=assembled_page' confirms section-editor is deliberately outside the assemble-gate.

[4] Why the tool-fork landmine does not fire here: LANDMINES '`section_edit` on a per-site TOOL FORK...' needs template fields AND empty content_data on the TARGET component; the target is the ported-page section component (content_data populated with provenance, template field {{.body}} only), not the tool slot — checked in bugs_open/277 §4 before this design, and the transform branch never renders a template at all, so the blank-every-text-node mechanism is structurally absent.

[5] Why inserting markup is safe where the stripper bans it: literal_markdown.go header scopes the ban to 'a converter that INSERTS markup would be writing into an unescaping pipe' — content_data values feeding text/template. The transform runs downstream on the pipe's output; inserted bytes are exactly '' and ''; interior class excludes <, >, backtick; and the dead-link repair (repairComponentHTMLBeforePersist, bugs_open/136) is standing precedent for deterministic HTML rewriting on this same persist path.

[6] The promoter interaction, measured not assumed: 444's live doors — EXISTS(>=1 complete for (item_type, handler_agent)) AND (sample<5 OR ratio>=25%). literal_markdown->section-editor has 0 completes, so it is HELD until a canary completes; the canary-by-hand precedent is commit 8d77196ad (083's first canary, ran end to end). The 7 current rows are all terminal (wont_fix 08-18 dispatch wave), so the detector's next sweep files fresh items at the new shape — dedup index confirmed to exclude all their statuses.

[7] Tests as run, 2026-08-20: go build ./platform/... green; go test on datahelpers, actions, discovery_checks, cmd/config-key-audit all green after the parity-literal bump; mutation runs: TagName reorder caught by the mixed-case case, skip-disable caught by 3 tests incl. the real fixture's script literal; migration 513 round-trip apply->rollback restored md5 fdb8cb4d40a17e471539c1df14e3b2a6 exactly, then applied for real (new md5 b6076c7d..., flag and whitelist verified at the column).
plan.risks: 1) A future rerender of a transformed component would regenerate from content_data and lose the edit — for this population that path is exactly what is refused today (the same un-regenerability that made them unrepairable makes the edit durable), and the 357 trigger archives any overwrite; stated in the action header rather than assumed. 2) The routing predicate could route a REGENERABLE component whose template fields the coarse regex missed — every miss direction was chosen to shrink the field list, which pushes toward 'can fill' and the old route; the residual (function-arg-only templates with rendered_html-source code_span findings on a once-occurring slot) keeps content_data's defect until its next regeneration re-files the finding, i.e. degrades to today's loop, not to damage. 3) The transform leaves detection-reachable-but-conversion-unreachable spans (crossing inline tags, entity-encoded backticks): converted==0 refuses loudly; partial conversion completes the edit and the whole-page verifier then FAILS the item into human review — no path stamps complete over a still-served finding. 4) The canary is a human step; until it runs, the 7 keep cycling the wont_fix loop they are in today — the close-out plan in bugs_open/277 names it so it cannot silently not-happen. 5) check.py's cluster copy keeps the old apply_section_edit count until the overlay is re-applied — owed post-commit, listed in the handoff.
